puzzle.instruction: Choose the token that keeps all three relationships.
puzzle.explanation: In the worked pair, the second token has a different shape and a different fill, and it sits one slot to the right of the first token. The highlighted option keeps all three relationships beside the query token. Every other choice is what a different shape, fill, and direction rule would predict, and each of those rules disagrees with the worked pair.

puzzle.instruction: The centre line is a fold. Apply the same unfolding to the new punch.
puzzle.explanation: The worked pair establishes the visible crease program: vertical:rightToLeft, then horizontal:bottomToTop. Opening each fold preserves every existing punch and adds its mirror across that crease, so one crease makes two punches and two creases make four. Applying the same complete program to the query gives the highlighted board. The distractors leave a fold closed, omit one crease, unfold across the wrong axis, or move the punch to its mirror instead of keeping both.

puzzle.instruction: Apply the same spatial transformation.
puzzle.explanation: The first pair shows that the complete arrangement moves one slot right, wrapping across the board edge. Both tokens keep their shapes and fills while their board positions change together. Applying that exact spatial rule to the third board gives the highlighted arrangement. Every distractor is the output of another bounded rotation, reflection, or wrapped shift that fails the worked pair.

puzzle.instruction: Apply both demonstrated relationship changes.
puzzle.explanation: The worked pair changes both relationship and position. First the loose token is placed inside a diamond; then the complete container moves one slot down and right. Repeating both visible changes on the third board gives the highlighted option. Each distractor uses a different container or movement program that fails the worked pair.

puzzle.instruction: The first pair undoes two changes. Which scene similarly precedes the third?
puzzle.explanation: The first pair is shown in reverse order: the second board becomes the first after the board rotates 2 quarter-turns clockwise and every fill advances 2 steps. Test each option as the missing input and apply both changes. Only the highlighted input produces the third board exactly. Each distractor would work under another bounded spatial-and-fill program, but that program fails the worked pair.

puzzle.instruction: Use the fold arrow and worked pair. Which folded punch produces the third board?
puzzle.explanation: Work backward from the open query board using the worked crease program: horizontal:bottomToTop. Mirrored punches overlap when each indicated side folds across its centre line, leaving the single punch shown by the highlighted folded board. Its punch position, crease axes, and arrows all match the worked pair. The other options use a different bounded fold program, so they either unfold to another pattern or contradict the demonstrated directions.

puzzle.instruction: Infer the row operation and the column operation. Which board satisfies both?
puzzle.explanation: The two directions use independently demonstrated set rules on matching board positions. Across each row, the third board keeps positions found in exactly one input. Down each column, the bottom board keeps every occupied position from either input. Applying both rules to the missing corner produces the same highlighted board; every distractor comes from a set rule that fails a worked row or column, from the right rule applied to the two boards in the wrong order, or from copying one of those two boards instead of combining them.

puzzle.instruction: Follow the worked gate paths, then apply the query gates from left to right.
puzzle.explanation: The three worked paths define the gates separately. The outline triangle rotates 1 quarter-turn clockwise. The solid square changes every token to solid without moving it. The half-filled diamond copies the token at the demonstrated source into the empty centre. Applying those gates from left to right gives the highlighted board. The distractors stop early, run the same gates in another order, or run a machine whose gates disagree with a worked path.

puzzle.instruction: Infer how the first two boards combine to make the third.

First, aligned positions are combined so the output keeps every occupied position from either input; then that result reflects left to right. Board positions and token identities make both steps visible. Applying the complete rule to the last pair gives the highlighted option. Each distractor comes from another set-and-spatial program that fails at least one worked row.

puzzle.instruction: Split the panels into two alternating rules. What comes next?
puzzle.explanation: Split the row into odd and even panels. In the odd-panel strand, the star token moves 3 perimeter slots counter-clockwise and cycles outline to half to solid; in the even-panel strand, the diamond token moves 2 perimeter slots counter-clockwise and cycles outline to half to solid. The missing panel belongs to the even strand, so applying its own position and fill rule once more gives the highlighted option. Each distractor is a prediction from another bounded step rule that fails the shown even transition.

Each distractor comes from another bounded direction, starting jump, or growth rule that fails a shown landing.
